business_rules.statement: The Command Center is Tier 3 of the platform's tier model: Tier 1 defines (Super Admin platform console), Tier 2 configures (Studio), Tier 3 runs (Command Center), the floor executes (Frontline Worker Application) against the record of truth (Delivery Operations Hub).
Boundary one — it authors nothing. The Command Center holds no configuration of its own; configuration originates in the Standards and Operations Studio.
business_rules.enforcement_point: No configuration write endpoint is exposed to this surface except the Lane B application path of section 21.9

business_rules.statement: Boundary two — it owns no record. Every Command Center action is a command executed through the owning Delivery Operations Hub service and written to the Delivery Operations Hub audit trail. There is no separate Command Center database.
business_rules.enforcement_point: All writes route through the owning service with the actor's identity

business_rules.statement: Boundary three — it is not the trace viewer. Agent internals stay platform-internal; the agent panel renders the activity summary and evidence list only.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Agent panel rendering; no Command Center endpoint returns orchestrator reasoning internals

business_rules.statement: The set of operational actions is closed at ten; adding an eleventh is a scope decision, never a drift.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Interface: an interaction that does not map to one of the ten is not offered at all

business_rules.statement: Scope resolution failure denies the action; it never degrades to a wider scope.
The service commits the change and its audit event in the same transaction, under the one-transaction audit guarantee: an action that cannot be audited does not happen.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Owning Delivery Operations Hub service transaction

business_rules.statement: Only a committed state is rendered as taken. Optimistic rendering of an uncommitted action is prohibited.
Where the change must reach a device, the Command Center renders the command's state honestly — created, queued, delivered, applied — never as an accomplished fact on the floor.
Captured evidence is immutable. Annotations are added to the record; the original reading is never changed.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Delivery Operations Hub append-only correction discipline

business_rules.statement: Idempotency: re-issuing the same action on the same record produces one committed effect and one audit entry.

Persist only non-suppressive preferences (column order, density, default landing tab); never persist a filter that can hide an item carrying an unacknowledged escalation or an open gate item; re-apply full visibility at every session start.
The Command Center reuses the five fixed tenant roles and the Tenant, Site and Area scoping defined platform-wide; it introduces no role types of its own.
Multi-role assignment is additive, and the audit log records identity and action, never "acting as role".
Scopes are Tenant, Site and Area, held simultaneously and orthogonally; Location (Cell), Job and worker-level scoping are deferred beyond V1.
Where no holder of a routed role is on shift, delivery falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, explicitly marked as a fallback delivery.
The landing view is a routing default, not a permission. A Quality Manager who lands on the decision queues must reach the live board in one navigation act.
The surface renders the freshness marker before it renders any aggregate, so that no number appears on screen without its age.
The Command Center is delivered as responsive web only. There is no separate native Command Center application. Push-class events reach every open session regardless of device.
The module map lists exactly thirteen modules; the count is validated against the source and matches the platform's numbers canon.
There is no user administration module, no configuration module, no audit-log-viewer module and no notification-preferences module on this surface.
Data owned by the Command Center: none, by charter. Only transient session state — current view, filter, selection, subscription position — exists; none is a record.
The surface emits no domain events of its own; a domain event is emitted by the owning service when a Command Center-originated command commits.

The command channel carries exactly five classes platform-wide: lot release; reassignment or substitution; qualification clearance; suspension; version change. The Command Center originates exactly three: lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance.
Command state must always be rendered honestly and never collapsed into "sent". The Command Center must never show an action as completed because the server created a command.
The Command Center carries no outbound integration to a tenant's own systems.
The Standards and Operations Studio receives exactly one class of write from the Command Center — an approved Lane B value change.
The Frontline Worker Application receives nothing directly from the Command Center; it receives command-channel actions at its next sync, and it is never remotely controlled.
The board does not claim the cell stopped, and does not pretend it can see it. Offline cells degrade gracefully to their last-synced picture with the marker showing its age.
No element implies the offline device received or applied anything. A command targeting that device renders as queued or available for delivery, never as delivered or applied.

Command Center session offline: Detect, do not guess; freeze and label, never blank; disable every decision control with the reason shown; queue nothing; name the alternate route; escalate the human, not the software.

No action is stored client-side for later transmission. The Frontline Worker Application queues because captures are facts about the past; the Command Center does not queue because decisions are instructions about the future.
No artificial-intelligence logic lives in the screen itself; intelligence is delivered to it by agents running beneath it. Detection is deterministic and interpretation is agentic.

No artificial-intelligence model sits in the deviation-triggering path; detection is rule-based and runs on the worker's device using the limits and severity mappings carried in the version-pinned work package; agents activate only after a deterministic trigger.

With no agents the surface remains useful and safe: board, alert feed, containment display and all ten operational actions remain fully functional; only interpretation, prior cases, new gate items, new Lane B proposals, coaching activations and the handoff brief are lost, and each is shown as lost.
A gate item raised before an emergency pause remains decidable during the pause; in-flight agent runs checkpoint at their next stage boundary and park; resume is a separate audited act.
No agent output is back-filled after an outage as though it had been produced on time; the gap is visible in the activity log.
FB-CC-AUTH: there is no degraded-authorisation mode; no cached role set ever admits a user or widens a scope.
In force is never displayed until every relevant device has confirmed.
A gate item with incomplete context is never made decidable by defaulting the missing element; it renders not decidable, never executes on its own and never silently expires.
The Delivery Operations Hub holds one immutable audit log per tenant, ingesting Studio publish events, Command Center decisions and Super Admin platform console access events.

Tenant isolation is absolute; nothing is shared across tenants and nothing becomes external training data. Encryption at rest and in transit are enforced platform invariants with no off position for any account including the root.

No break-glass path exists on the Command Center; there is no ambient browsing anywhere on the console, and support access into tenant context is read-only, reason-required, ticket-linked, time-boxed and tenant-visible with an End-session control.
The Command Center is live to the server's knowledge, and it says so. Every live element shows how fresh its data is. Offline is a displayed state, never a hidden failure.
No visual treatment, no summarisation and no simplification may remove a freshness marker from an element that carries one.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Acceptance criteria, not the style guide

business_rules.statement: Every element on the surface belongs to exactly one of three freshness classes: Pushed (event), Refreshed (state), On-sync (eventual).
business_rules.enforcement_point: Design-time class assignment recorded in the element's specification

business_rules.statement: The pushed class's honest latency is measured from server receipt, not from the event happening on the floor; the platform never implies it knew at the device time.
Every tile and every drill view carries a compact sync-state element; selecting the marker lists the devices behind the number and when each was last seen.
The marker never reports a pending-capture count of zero for a device whose pending count is unknown; it reports unknown.
The board never goes blank because the floor went dark: it shows the last truth, and its timestamp.
Every aggregate carries an as-of timestamp; record-level views flag late-arriving captures explicitly. No number a supervisor may have acted on is ever silently rewritten.

Where late data materially changes the headline figures of a closed shift or a finished record, the recompute is itself an audited event. The platform default for materiality is any change to a severity count.
A partially completed recompute is never rendered; the previous value and stamp persist instead.
Run completion has three distinct meanings kept separate: submitted, complete, finished. Submitted is the state the board displays and supervisors act on.
Finish is the one automatic transition on the platform; the run auto-close scheduler finishes the run automatically and its figures are final.

Manual close is a run-lifecycle act executed on the Delivery Operations Hub run record, linked from the Command Center drill; it is deliberately not one of the ten operational actions and requires a mandatory note.

The board's four-part information contract: (1) where attention is needed, ranked by severity; (2) what is running normally, compressed to almost no visual cost; (3) what the platform cannot currently see — the sync state; and (4) one gesture from noticed to full context.
Exception-first: normal operation compresses to a quiet summary band and the screen gives its space to whatever needs a person. A floor where nothing is wrong is a quiet screen, at any scale.
The board's rendering cost must scale with the exception count, not the cell count. The summary band is a real aggregation, not a styling choice.
Cell status equals the highest active severity among that cell's open deviations, with a distinct coaching-active state strictly below deviation level. The Command Center adds no rules of its own.
Pace is evaluated as screens complete, at the screen boundary — never continuously. Timing expectations are optional; a workflow without them shows no pace state.
Pace is informational and supervisor-only. It triggers nothing by itself and is never worker-facing: no pace state, flag, or timer derived from it is ever rendered on the Frontline device.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Payload inspection to the Frontline Worker Application

business_rules.statement: Out-of-scope Areas are absent from the server response, not filtered client-side.
The Plant Manager view is the same board at wider scope, not a separate executive-dashboard product.
The drill path is Board → cell view → run view → step or record detail. One gesture per level; full context at the bottom.
A run finishes on the workflow version it started on, and in-flight runs are never re-based.

Exception-led, never surveillance: the default board shows Locations (Cells) and lines, never individual workers. Worker-level detail appears on drill — opened from an exception, a pushed alert, or an approval item — never as a default wall of per-worker feeds.
There is no route, filter, search or saved view on this surface whose entry point is a worker. A worker's name is always an attribute of an event, never an axis of navigation.
Worker-level data is held as purpose-bound aggregates — qualification state, readiness flags, trends — not raw per-worker behavioural feeds.
Completed work older than the current shift belongs to the Delivery Operations Hub. An active multi-day run always shows on the board, regardless of its age.
business_rules.enforcement_point: History boundary, implemented as a hard rule rather than a default filter

business_rules.statement: A step not yet received renders distinctly from a step not done, because those are different claims.

The agent interprets; it never classifies. Classification happened on the device, at the instant of capture, including offline, using the limits and severity mappings carried in the version-pinned work package.
The containment checklist is policy — selected by configuration, never invented by the agent — and launches locally on the device at classification, offline-capable.
A Severity 1 event freezes the lot automatically — on the device, at classification, even offline; the server-side path mirrors, it never triggers.

Where a Job declares no Lot entity, the Severity 1 freeze lands on the Lot where a lot exists, the Unit where work is serialized, otherwise the Run, whose output is quarantined and the run blocked pending Quality Manager disposition.
business_rules.enforcement_point: No-lot rule applied on-device at classification

business_rules.statement: Evidence is immutable; the Command Center displays, never edits. A reviewer who challenges a capture's validity adds an append-only annotation; the original is never altered.

Releasing a Severity 1 hold takes human authority — Quality Manager only, uniformly, with no exception by work type, risk class or tag. Supervisors request release with a note, and the request lands as an item for the Quality Manager.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Delivery Operations Hub lot service; refused at the service for any other identity

business_rules.statement: Marking evidence reviewed is an audited action carried onto the Delivery Operations Hub review queue, so the same capture never demands a duplicate look on the back office.
When the platform cannot process a release, containment persists: the hold remains in force. No queued release fires by itself.

A reasoning agent produces an output and needs no gate. An action agent proposes an intervention that changes state or reaches a worker, and that proposal passes through a human approval gate before it takes effect.
Some action-agent steps are pre-authorised policy — a configured checklist launching, a configured escalation firing. The gate exists for proposed interventions beyond pre-authorised policy.

Adopted position 2026-08-14: gating is declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field, whose declared values are `authoring-time policy`, `runtime human gate`, and `none — reasoning agent`.

The gate card leads with the scope of impact — how many pieces, runs and jobs the intervention touches — because a decider without it will either rubber-stamp or stall. An item whose scope of impact cannot be computed is rendered not decidable.

Three gate decisions: Approve; Adjust within bounds and approve; Decline with a categorised reason. Adjust-and-approve is a first-class action rather than a forced decline-and-wait. Every decision is two interactions — the decision, plus an optional note.

Bounds means a decider may adjust the scope of the proposed intervention, not convert it into a different intervention type, and not extend it beyond what the policy permits that intervention to reach.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Interface refuses the adjustment and directs the decider to decline

business_rules.statement: A waiting gate item never executes on its own and never silently expires; it re-routes to the next person on timeout.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Studio-authored acknowledge, timeout and fallback discipline, server-side

business_rules.statement: Approving a newly composed agent for live use is an authoring-time control belonging to the Studio's approval chain plus platform review — it is never an in-shift decision and never appears in this queue.
The scope of impact should be computed deterministically from records rather than estimated by the agent.

Learning divides into two lanes by a single test: does it alter a configured operating value? Lane A no — applied automatically, logged, reversible. Lane B yes — always surfaced as evidence-backed proposals for human approval, never auto-approved.
The platform never invents content, rules or thresholds in either lane. Lane B carries value-level changes only; authoring never rides the learning pipeline.
Undecided Lane B proposals age visibly; after 30 days a stale flag copies to the Quality Manager's digest. Proposals never silently expire.
The package test: package-borne values auto-publish a patch version on approval and distribute per adoption timing, with no second approval; server-only values apply immediately on approval.
A Lane B change is never auto-approved — a person always decides; once decided, publication is platform machinery. The decision is always human; the publication is automatic and fully audited.
Every applied Lane B change appears in the Studio change log attributed "approved by [user] on agent proposal".
Learning is on by default and the approval queue is the control; no learning on-off switch exists anywhere on this surface.
A proposal whose affected field's package assignment is not enumerated renders not decidable; the decision is withheld rather than guessed.
Where publication ultimately cannot complete, the decision remains audited and the configured value remains unchanged — an approval is not an effect.
Every decision is a teaching event; all three learning loops refine selection, ranking and proposal quality on top of the rules the tenant's team authored, and all three are isolated per tenant.
A Lane B approval teaches the platform nothing automatically; what is remembered is the decline and its reason.
Feedback on agent outputs is always optional and one tap — never required, never gating. No interaction may be blocked pending feedback and no feedback control may be modal.
A learning signal must never block a governed decision; on learning-store failure the decision commits regardless and the signal is recorded as pending.
Switching an agent is a Standards and Operations Studio action, linked from the agent panel, never performed there.

The activity log test: a plant manager reads an entry and understands what the agent did and why, without an engineer in the room. An entry requiring knowledge of atoms, orchestrator stages or model behaviour has failed it.
An agent failing is flagged immediately in plain terms; persistent degradation — a second consecutive failure, or any failure outlasting a shift — escalates to the Plant Manager view.
Degradation visible across more than one tenant is a platform incident owned in the Super Admin platform console; the tenant-facing panel keeps showing the honest per-tenant flag throughout.
Every pushed event lands in the feed, filterable by Area, severity, type and state.

Escalation routing is a structured record per severity level authored in the Studio and resolved by the Delivery Operations Hub to the people actually on shift. Routing keys to roles, never individuals, with de-duplication; there is no on-call calendar at V1.
A fallback is visibly marked as a fallback — the original target's miss is recorded, not hidden, and the Shift Handoff Agent carries it into the end-of-shift brief.

Acknowledge means "I have seen this and own it"; resolve means "it is dealt with". Both are explicit, timestamped actions on the Delivery Operations Hub-owned record. Acknowledgement is one state on the record, writable from in-app or email, never a channel-local store.

Escalation and alert notifications are delivered in-app and by email — exactly these two channels, platform-wide. In-app notifications cannot be muted. SMS, OS push, webhooks, external recipients and quiet hours are outside V1.

All on-shift holders of the routed role at the Location are notified, and the first acknowledgement claims the item. The platform never lets an escalation resolve to no one, and never pretends a fallback was the plan.
At qualification expiry the worker may complete the current run and the next assignment is blocked, enforced at step level on the device.
No filter can hide an item carrying an unacknowledged escalation from the actor responsible for it.
Email acknowledgement links must be single-use and identity-bound so that forwarding an email cannot transfer authority.

No fallback path bypasses role-based access control, crosses tenants, bypasses qualification, specification, evaluation, approval or publication controls, or bypasses the Severity 1 hold and release rules.
No fallback path enters an unbounded retry loop.
The refresh interval accepts 60 seconds as default, accepts values down to 30 seconds subject to scale validation, and rejects values below 30 seconds rather than clamping silently.
The surface exposes exactly thirteen modules; no fourteenth module route exists.
The surface originates commands in exactly three of the five command-channel classes: lot release, reassignment or substitution, and qualification clearance.
On session transport loss, the surface freezes with a labelled banner within five seconds, disables every decision control and stores no action client-side.
Rendering cost and payload size scale with the exception count, not the cell count, verified at 8, 47 and 120 cells.
No pace state, flag or derived timer is present in any payload reaching the Frontline Worker Application.

decisions.question: Delivery Operations Hub against "Digital Operations Hub" — which surface name is canonical?
options: Delivery Operations Hub (Statement of Work)
Digital Operations Hub (blueprint commission)
decisions.adopted_working_position: The surface name used throughout this blueprint for the record-of-truth surface is Delivery Operations Hub, per the Statement of Work
decisions.status: Registered; unresolved naming divergence, not silently reconciled
decisions.impact: Surface naming across every artefact

decisions.question: The two differing seven-type capture lists — which set of seven capture types is authoritative?
options: The §5.5.3 set
The other seven-type list
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopted on the §5.5.3 set, with both readings retained in the card
decisions.status: Registered; adopted working position, only client ratification remains
decisions.impact: Studio builds against a settled set of seven capture types

decisions.question: Action-agent gating: pre-authorised policy against a runtime human gate for every action agent?
options: (a) confirm the pre-authorised-policy reading and correct the console Part's wording
(b) confirm the every-action-gated reading and remove pre-authorised policy, accepting queue volume
(c) define a third position in which pre-authorisation is itself the gate, recorded at authoring time
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopted position, 2026-08-14: option (c) — gating is declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field, whose declared values are `authoring-time policy`, `runtime human gate`, and `none — reasoning agent`. The Prevention Agent is bound to `authoring-time policy`; the Deviation and Containment Agent is bound to `runtime human gate` for proposals beyond pre-authorised containment.
decisions.status: Registered; adopted 2026-08-14 as a per-agent governance-binding declaration
decisions.impact: Gate queue volume; whether every coaching activation raises a gate item

decisions.question: Plant Manager listed as a fixed role, against the platform's exactly-five-fixed-tenant-roles canon?
options: Plant Manager becomes a sixth role
Plant Manager stays a persona plus a Tenant-scoped read grant
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint treats Plant Manager and Quality Director as personas — a scope shape layered on an existing role — not as role types; recommendation is persona plus a Tenant-scoped read grant
decisions.impact: Five-role canon, additive multi-role model, every authority matrix

decisions.question: The meaning of the `Supervisor+` and `Quality Manager+` shorthand across five additive, non-hierarchical roles.
options: Reading A: a rank ordering (Worker < Supervisor < Quality Manager < Tenant Admin)
Reading B: a set enumeration — the union of the named grants
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint uses reading B and enumerates the role set for every action, marking each use with `DEC-PLUS-001`. Recommendation: adopt reading B and publish an explicit per-action role set, retiring the "+" notation.
decisions.impact: Whether a Tenant Admin holding no operational role can acknowledge an escalation

decisions.question: Three-stage approval chain against Lane-B auto-publication of a patch version with no second approval.
options: (a) Quality Manager's Lane B approval satisfies the Release Authority stage
(b) require the full three-stage chain for Lane B changes, accepting the delay
(c) restrict Lane B auto-publish to values that cannot alter a specification limit or a severity mapping
decisions.impact: Whether a package-borne value change reaching a device has passed one human or three

decisions.question: Library pointer propagation against package pinning.

package pinning

decisions.question: The nobody-on-shift escalation default — confirm fallback to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift?

the client specifies a different fallback target

decisions.question: Browser support, minimum viewport and session timeout for the Command Center, all Not specified in the Statement of Work.
options: (a) evergreen browsers only, 1024-pixel minimum width, 30-minute idle timeout

(c) tenant-configurable idle timeout above a platform floor

decisions.question: What the Command Center does when its own browser session loses connectivity — Not specified in the Statement of Work.
options: (a) as specified, no client-side queueing — recommended
(b) allow client-side queueing of non-authority acts only
(c) allow full queueing with a server-side staleness check on arrival
decisions.adopted_working_position: Option (a): detect not guess; freeze and label, never blank; disable every decision control; queue nothing; name the alternate route; escalate the human, not the software
decisions.impact: Whether a stale queued authority action can ever fire

decisions.question: Is the 30-second refresh floor a protective platform limit, or an unnamed exception to the universal configurability principle? And who validates faster-than-default intervals?
options: (a) hard reject below 30 seconds with an explanatory message
(b) accept and clamp to 30 seconds with a visible notice
(c) allow below 30 seconds subject to a scale validation with named criteria and a named validating authority
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: option (a) plus an explicit statement in the platform floor register that this is a performance limit and not a safety floor, and a named validation owner for the 30-to-60-second range
decisions.impact: Whether a tenant requesting a 15-second board is rejected, throttled, or served degraded

decisions.question: The record-finish window's floor and ceiling — open drafting value against settled values.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The refreshed-state pipeline stalls; aggregate age exceeds two refresh intervals
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Keep the last successful values and change the marker to show the age explicitly; a bounded user-requested immediate refresh is available
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The affected module shows a no-current-data state naming the unreachable service
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Module-level degraded display with age; where the board, alert feed and gate queue are all degraded, the whole-surface honest banner and every decision control disabled
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on first successful read; values recompute and, where a severity count changed, the recompute is an audited event

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The pushed-event transport is lost while the session is otherwise healthy
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Degrade to polling at the tenant's refresh interval and say so, naming the time of the last received event
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Polling fails; the session enters FB-CC-SESS
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: As FB-CC-SESS — the frozen labelled board
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resubscribe and request every event since the last received event identifier; gap events are delivered and marked delivered-late with origin and display times; a pushed event is never skipped and ordering within a record's event sequence is preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: This session loses the platform (transport loss detected from the push channel and failed refresh calls, not a browser network flag)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Freeze, label, disable every decision control with the reason shown, queue nothing, name the alternate route
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The transport does not return within a bounded interval and the tablet cannot reach the platform at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The frozen labelled board with all decision controls disabled — it can mislead nobody and blocks no floor activity
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resubscribe from the last received event identifier and replay the gap, marking replayed events delivered-late; nothing was queued so there is nothing to reconcile client-side

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An operational action's service call fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The action is not rendered as taken; the control returns to its pre-action state with an explicit message naming the service and the time of the attempt, and one bounded retry is offered as a deliberate act
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The action did not happen and the user has been told so, with the alternate route named (the same act on the Delivery Operations Hub's own screens)
failures_fallbacks.recovery: No queued action fires automatically; the user re-issues it deliberately; idempotent writes make a re-issue safe and a duplicate is refused

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A command reaches the channel but not the device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The surface continues to render the honest per-device state — issued, propagating, with each device's confirmation timestamp — and does not escalate on its own
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The hold remains in force on every device that confirmed and remains unconfirmed on the absent device; the absent device's own on-device Severity 1 freeze persists locally
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On the device's return the command applies in order and the state advances; propagation lag is metered as platform telemetry. Related open decision: DEC-SYNC-001

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Agent output is unavailable or degraded
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Plain-language unavailability statement naming what was not produced and that platform operations has been notified
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Persistent degradation — a second consecutive failure, or any failure outlasting a shift
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No-agent operating mode with every deterministic function intact; persistent degradation escalates to the Plant Manager view
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Fixing an agent is a Studio or platform action linked from the panel; no retroactive back-fill — outputs the agent would have produced are not back-filled as though they had existed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Identity, role or scope resolution fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Deny. There is no degraded-authorisation mode, because authorisation sits above continuity in the fallback safety priority order
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Repeated resolution failure across the tenant
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The session does not open, or the open session is closed at the next authorisation checkpoint; the Delivery Operations Hub and Frontline Worker Application are unaffected and the floor continues
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Normal session opening when resolution returns; no session is auto-restored with pre-failure authority; denial events are audited so an outage is visible rather than inferred

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Report generation or scheduled delivery fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The on-demand request returns an explicit failure naming the data set and the as-of time attempted; no partial file is offered
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A failed scheduled delivery is retried once at a bounded interval and then reported as a failed delivery, never silently skipped
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No file delivered, delivery recorded as failed, recipients notified in-app that the scheduled report did not arrive
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The next scheduled delivery includes the corrections, flagged as corrections; material corrections trigger an audited recompute and the per-format re-send option applies

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An approval-queue item cannot render its required context (scope of impact or evidence unresolvable; indeterminate package assignment for a Lane B field)
